'''Teta''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[duke]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> who was [[Marriage|married]] to the younger [[Twi'lek]] [[Koyi Mateil]]. Mateil secretly hoped for her husband to [[Death|die]] so that she could inherit his fortune. Teta and his wife visited the<ref name="Die Wanna Wanga" /> the [[Galaxies Opera House]] in the [[Uscru District]] of the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]]<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> in the [[Standard year|year]] [[19 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY]].</ref> during a performance of the [[opera]] ''[[Squid Lake]]''.<ref name="USW" /> The two were walking up the opera house's steps behind<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> the [[alien]] [[Opula Deget]] and the human [[Ulfor Bombaasa]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> when the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] ran past them on his way to meet with [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]].<ref name="ROTS" /> Teta had fair skin and [[Color|brown]] [[eye]]s. The duke wore a teal and mustard colored [[Clothing|opera coat]] and [[Hat|headpiece]] while on Coruscant.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
Teta first appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="ROTS" /> which released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].<ref name="YBY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Concept art of the character was drawn by artist [[Sang Jun Lee]].<ref name="ArtOf">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> The opera steps scene was filmed on R Stage at [[Shepperton Studios]] as part of additional photography on Monday, [[August 23]], [[2004]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was first named by the article "Die Wanna Wanga: Encounters of The Twi'lek Kind", written by [[Tim Veekhoven]] and posted on [[StarWars.com]] on [[August 19]], [[2014]].<ref name="Die Wanna Wanga" /> The character's name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the reference book ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'', which was written by [[Trisha Biggar]]<ref name="DressingAGalaxy">''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]''</ref> and released on [[October 11]], 2005.<ref name="DressingDate">{{WebCite|url=https://www.waterstones.com/book/dressing-a-galaxy-part-1/trisha-biggar/george-lucas/9780810959644|text=Dressing a Galaxy: Part 1: The Costumes of Star Wars (Hardback)|work=[[Wikipedia:Waterstones|Waterstones]]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/mxQvt|archivedate=2022-04-24}}</ref>
